findings.title: Malicious process p.exe executing from C:\Windows\Temp\Perfmon\
findings.description: p.exe (PID 8260) is running from C:\Windows\Temp\Perfmon\p.exe. The use of a temp directory disguised as a performance monitoring path is a classic masquerading technique (T1036.005). The process was launched at 2018-08-30 22:15:18 UTC and remains active at image capture time.
findings.evidence: windows.pstree shows p.exe (PID 8260) at path c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe, created 2018-08-30 22:15:18 UTC, still running. windows.filescan confirms file object at \Windows\Temp\Perfmon\p.exe and directory \Windows\Temp\Perfmon.
findings.mitre: T1036.005 - Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location

findings.title: WMI-initiated PowerShell execution chain leading to implant deployment
findings.description: WmiPrvSE.exe (PID 2876) spawned powershell.exe (PID 8712) at 2018-08-30 16:43:36 UTC. Powershell (8712) then spawned a second PowerShell (PID 5848) with arguments '-Version 5.1 -s -NoLogo -NoProfile' (server-mode remoting session). This PS session ultimately launched cmd.exe (PID 5948) with the command 'C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe /C c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe' at 2018-08-30 22:15:18 UTC.
findings.evidence: windows.pstree and windows.cmdline output: WmiPrvSE (2876) -> powershell (8712) -> powershell (5848, args: -Version 5.1 -s -NoLogo -NoProfile) -> cmd (5948, args: /C c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe) -> p.exe (8260)
findings.mitre: T1047 - WMI; T1059.001 - PowerShell; T1569.002 - System Services

findings.title: Domain Admin credentials used by attacker-controlled processes
findings.description: p.exe (PID 8260), powershell (PID 8712), and powershell (PID 5848) all run under account 'spsql' (SID S-1-5-21-3445421715-2530590580-3149308974-1193), which is a member of Domain Admins (S-1-5-21-3445421715-2530590580-3149308974-512) and Administrators (S-1-5-32-544) at High Mandatory Level. The name 'spsql' suggests a SQL Server service account was compromised for this attack.
findings.evidence: windows.getsids output for PIDs 8260, 8712, 5848 all show spsql with Domain Admins membership.

findings.title: Active C2 communication to 172.16.4.10:8080
findings.description: Multiple TCP connections (ESTABLISHED and CLOSE_WAIT) observed between the victim (172.16.6.11) and 172.16.4.10 on port 8080. Three connections remain ESTABLISHED at capture time; seven additional CLOSE_WAIT connections indicate sustained beaconing activity over an extended period. No owning PID is attributed by netscan, consistent with connections made by a process that has since cycled its connection handles or with network stack state retention after process activity.
findings.evidence: windows.netscan: offsets 0x8c88af069cb0, 0x8c88b7f274c0, 0x8c88b9076010 show ESTABLISHED TCPv4 to 172.16.4.10:8080; seven additional CLOSE_WAIT entries to same endpoint.
findings.mitre: T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols; T1571 - Non-Standard Port

findings.title: Multiple rundll32 executions with no arguments from attacker-controlled PowerShell
findings.description: PowerShell (PID 5848) spawned at least 6 rundll32.exe instances (PIDs 6768, 5452, 5588, 2216, 4108, 8148) with no command-line arguments visible. All exited within seconds to minutes. Rundll32 without arguments is a classic hollow-process or code-injection carrier. p.exe (PID 8260) additionally spawned 3 rundll32.exe instances (PIDs 5768, 7552, 1424) across multiple days.
findings.evidence: windows.pstree shows rundll32 children of PID 5848 and PID 8260; windows.cmdline shows all with empty argument fields.

findings.title: Large RWX memory region in p.exe indicative of in-memory payload
findings.description: windows.malfind identified a 481-page (approximately 1.88 MB) PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE private VAD region in p.exe (PID 8260) at virtual address range 0x2be0000-0x2dc0fff with no file backing. This is a primary indicator of an in-memory shellcode or reflectively-loaded payload.
findings.evidence: windows.malfind: PID 8260 p.exe, VPN 0x2be0000-0x2dc0fff, VadS, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, CommitCharge=481, PrivateMemory=1.
findings.mitre: T1055 - Process Injection; T1620 - Reflective Code Loading

findings.title: p.exe DLL load profile matches C2 implant with post-load capability expansion
findings.description: p.exe loaded WININET.dll (HTTP/S), WS2_32.dll, DNSAPI.dll (network stack), CRYPTSP.dll, rsaenh.dll, bcrypt.dll (crypto stack), Secur32.dll, SSPICLI.DLL (credential APIs) at startup. Critically, mpr.dll (network drive/redirector API), USER32.dll, GDI32.dll loaded approximately 6 days after initial execution (2018-09-05 12:13-12:14 UTC), indicating the implant downloaded and activated additional modules during its 7-day dwell time.
findings.evidence: windows.dlllist --pid 8260: initial DLLs loaded at 2018-08-30 22:15:18-19 UTC; mpr.dll LoadTime=2018-09-05 12:13:26 UTC; USER32/GDI32/etc LoadTime=2018-09-05 12:14:36 UTC.
findings.mitre: T1071.001 - C2 over HTTP; T1573 - Encrypted Channel

findings.title: Lateral movement to 172.16.4.5 via RDP and SMB
findings.description: Multiple closed RDP connections observed from the victim (172.16.6.11) to 172.16.4.5:3389, plus one ESTABLISHED SMB connection to 172.16.4.5:445. A second SMB connection to 172.16.7.15:445 was also established. An LDAP query to 172.16.4.4:389 (likely a domain controller) indicates Active Directory reconnaissance. Incoming SMB connection from 172.16.6.14:65368 suggests the compromised host was also accessed by another attacker-controlled host.
findings.evidence: windows.netscan: CLOSED RDP to 172.16.4.5:3389 (multiple), ESTABLISHED SMB to 172.16.4.5:445 and 172.16.7.15:445, CLOSED LDAP to 172.16.4.4:389, ESTABLISHED incoming SMB from 172.16.6.14:65368.
findings.mitre: T1021.001 - RDP; T1021.002 - SMB/Windows Admin Shares

findings.title: No registry-based persistence detected
findings.description: windows.registry.printkey on SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and RunOnce revealed no malicious entries. Only legitimate Run entries for OneDrive, Dashlane, and DashlanePlugin under the tdungan user profile. No malware-associated services found in windows.svcscan in user-writable paths.
findings.evidence: windows.registry.printkey on Run and RunOnce keys; windows.svcscan output grep for temp/appdata/users returned no suspicious entries.

findings.title: F-Response forensic collection tool present (investigator artifact)
findings.description: subject_srv.exe (PID 1096) running as C:\windows\subject_srv.exe with arguments connecting to base-hunt.shieldbase.lan:5682. This is the F-Response Subject utility used by the investigator for remote memory acquisition. Started 2018-09-06 18:28:30 UTC, approximately 29 minutes before image capture. Connection 172.16.6.11:3262 -> 172.16.5.50:39372 ESTABLISHED corresponds to this service.
findings.evidence: windows.pstree and windows.cmdline: subject_srv.exe with -s base-hunt.shieldbase.lan:5682 -v 'F-Response Subject'; windows.svcscan confirms F-Response Subject service. netscan shows ESTABLISHED connection to 172.16.5.50:39372.
